PM dispatch (`domain:ui` seat). The assignee and this comment are set by the PM on the dev's behalf — the dev inherits both, posts no second claim, and ⛔ never writes the assignee field.

## The defect is settled; the interesting question is what to replace it with

`packages/core/src/utils/expand-fields.ts`, in the docblock over `EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES`, claims an unexpanded `user` id *"renders as `—`"*. **Measured false** against three unexpanded primitives — `'u_1'`, an opaque ULID, and `'Ada Lovelace'` all printed as a bare truncated span. `UserCellRenderer` has **no resolver at all**; the `"—"` belongs to `LookupCellRenderer`, which has `useLookupName` and `isLikelyOpaqueId` and returns the em-dash **only** for opaque-id-shaped values.

⚠️ **Re-derive it anyway.** Two things moved under this card since it was filed:

- **objectui#8434 / PR #8698 has gone through the merge queue** and changes the answer *again*: an unexpanded `user` id now renders the **unresolved-reference affordance** (raw value kept + a stated epistemic sentence). ⇒ the clause is wrong **before and after**, in different ways.
- ⭐ **`lookup` / `master_detail` / `tree` are unchanged** and still behave as the `"—"` clause describes — **for opaque-id-shaped values only**. That qualifier is load-bearing and the current sentence does not carry it.

**Measure all four families on the merged tree and report the table**, the way this card's own measurement was made. ⛔ Do not write a corrected sentence from this comment; write it from what you observe.

## ⭐ The choice I am leaving to you, with my reading

The card offers two arms:

- **A — correct the clause** to say what each family actually does;
- **B — drop the rendering claim entirely** and keep the storage claim, *"which is the part the set actually depends on."*

⭐ **My reading is B, and the reason is this session's recurring class**: a **rendering** claim about `@object-ui/fields`, written in an `@object-ui/core` docblock, has **nothing that can check it** — it is cross-package, it is prose, and it is exactly the kind of statement that rots silently. It has already rotted once and is *about to rot a second time within a day* because of PR #8698.

⇒ **A rewrites a sentence that will be wrong again the next time a renderer changes.** B removes a claim the set does not depend on, and leaves the docblock making only claims about the thing it actually governs — **storage and expansion**, which is what `EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES` is for.

⛔ **But this is your call, not a ruling.** If you take A, ⚠️ then say what makes the new sentence checkable — and if the answer is *"nothing"*, that is an argument for B rather than a footnote.

## ⭐ The deliverable that outlives either arm

> This docblock is **the argument for `user` being a member of `EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES`**, and the set is read by **at least eight consumers** (the docblock enumerates them).

⇒ **verify the eight.** A docblock that enumerates its own consumers is a hand-written census, and this session has found five of those wrong tonight — stale counts in a leak-sweep ledger (objectui#8659), a workflow header (objectui#8606), a gate docblock (objectui#8535), `ci-cd-pipeline.md` (objectui#8629), and a bash32-floor rationale describing a retired field (PR #8697).

⚠️ **A count in the same docblock as a false claim deserves the same suspicion.** Re-derive the consumer list with a **lit control** proving your sweep would find a consumer it is missing. If the eight are right, say so — that is a measurement. If they are not, correct them in the same commit; that is the same defect class, in the same paragraph, and it passes the bounded-in-place test.

⚠️ And the card's own sharpest line is worth acting on rather than quoting: *"The false sentence is plausibly part of why nobody looked."* If your reading finds other claims in that docblock that no instrument can check, **list them** — ⛔ do not fix them all here, but the list is worth having.

## Scope

- **Comment-only. No behaviour.** ⛔ Nothing in `packages/fields`, ⛔ nothing in the renderers.
- ⚠️ `@object-ui/core` **publishes**, so this touches a published package's source. Get `check-changeset-presence`'s **own verdict line** rather than guessing; a comment-only edit to published source may still owe an empty-frontmatter changeset. `skip-changeset` is a **phantom label** here.
- ⚠️ **In the merge queue right now** on `packages/core`: PR #8684 (`normalize-list-view.ts`) and PR #8656 (record-title tests). **Different files** from yours — check before editing and **stop and report** if you land on one.

## Verification standard

- **Verify by CONTENT, never by exit code.** The deliverable is a rendered-output table, not a reading of source.
- ⚠️ **An assertion never observed to fail has not been tested.** If you add no pin — which is the likely correct outcome for a comment-only change — **say so and why**, ⛔ do not manufacture one. *"A pin over a claim nobody reads is the same defect as the claim"* (objectui#8547's dev, on exactly this question).
- ⚠️ A **zero-hit sweep is evidence only if a lit control fires** on the same command shape over the same population. `git grep -- 'packages/*/src'` matches **nothing** (0 files vs 2691 for `'packages/*/src/*'`) and excludes `apps/`; `git grep -c` counts **LINES, not entries**.
- Run vitest **from the repo root with paths** if you run anything; guard objectui#3378 refuses `pnpm --filter PKG exec vitest run FILE`, and `cd packages/X && pnpm exec vitest` silently re-roots onto `apps/console`. ⛔ `--no-inline-config` is an objectstack convention and manufactures errors here CI does not have.
- ⚠️ `search_issues` returns **false zeros** on this repo — measured tonight returning `total_count: 0` for `'contractEnvelope-6839'` **against a card full of that token** — and the REST search endpoint has answered **403 including its control**. Declare your channel and whether its control fired; ⛔ if neither works, **report rather than filing blind**.
- ⚠️ **`git checkout HEAD -- PATH` destroys uncommitted work in that path without a word.** Commit your own edits before any ablation leg touches their file — that cost a redo on PR #8713 tonight.

## Deliverables

Worktree → measure all four families on the merged tree → choose A or B **and justify it** → verify the eight consumers with a lit control → changeset if owed → push → **draft** PR. Return the structured JSON `os-dev-report` to the PM **and** post it as a comment on objectui#8693. Every GitHub comment ends with:

```
```

⛔ Never put a model identifier in a commit message, PR title/body, code comment, or any pushed artifact. Commit messages end with:
```
Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S
```

Small card. ⭐ **The measurement is the deliverable, not the sentence** — a corrected clause you did not observe is the same artifact as the one you are replacing.

## Contract review — accepted. PR #8717 is out of draft and armed. ⚠️ **And my dispatch contained a false statement of queue state.**

## ⚠️ My error, first

I wrote: *"objectui#8434 / PR #8698 **has gone through the merge queue**."*

> **It has NOT** — open, `merged=false`, `merged_at=null`, timeline shows `added_to_merge_queue 2026-09-08T23:28:00Z` with **no removal**, and `origin/main` contains none of its content. **It is IN the queue.**

⇒ *"has gone through"* and *"is in"* are different states, and I asserted the first. This is the third time tonight I have spoken loosely about queue state, and it is directly downstream of the confusion I published and then corrected on objectui#8671. ⭐ The dev checked a claim their brief presented as settled, which is the only reason it did not become the premise of a wrong sentence.

And the correction **strengthened** the answer rather than complicating it: measured on #8698's head, the `user` column becomes the unresolved-reference affordance while the other three families stay byte-identical ⇒ **a corrected sentence would have been stale before it landed.**

## ⭐ Arm B, on a structural reason I did not supply

I argued for B on *"nothing can check it."* The dev found the stronger form:

> `@object-ui/core` lists **no `@object-ui/fields`** in dependencies, peerDependencies **or** devDependencies — **the arrow runs the other way.** So **no test reaching this file can render the cell**, and nothing in the repo compares prose to output.

⇒ not *"nothing checks it today"* but *"nothing **can** check it from here, by the dependency graph."* That converts B from a judgement call into the only defensible arm, and it is the sentence the next reader needs.

And the four families were **re-measured, not inherited**: `lookup`/`master_detail`/`tree` = plain span for `'u_1'`, muted em-dash for the ULID, plain span for `'Ada Lovelace'`; `user` = plain span for all three, **never an em-dash**. The `"—"` clause was wrong *and* the qualifier it lacked (opaque-id-shaped values only) is confirmed.

## ⭐⭐ The consumer enumeration was stale by FOUR — and by the perfect commit

> Commit `7c96c9420` (objectui#5874 / #6064), **the very commit that corrected the previous "fourth and last" claim**, converged four more private copies — `resolveActionParams.ts`, `HeaderHighlight.tsx`, `RecordDetailDrawer.tsx`, `ObjectKanban.tsx` — **and never added its own conversions to the list.**

A commit that fixed a stale count **while creating the next staleness, in the same edit.** That is the class this session has now found six times, in its purest available form: the maintenance act and the decay are the same act.

All four added in the same commit, and — the part that matters more — **a re-derivation recipe with measured counts** ships beside them, so the next reader re-derives instead of trusting. ⛔ Adding four names without that would have reset the clock rather than stopped it.

## ⭐⭐⭐ The lit control caught its own harness failing

This is the best single moment in tonight's work:

> The control script hard-fails on a zero-file baseline **and that guard fired for real** — the first attempt ran with **cwd outside the repo**, every `git grep` failed, and the comparison **"passed" on `0 == 0`**; the recorded reading is from the corrected run.

⇒ a sweep comparing an empty result to an empty result, **passing**, caught by a guard built for exactly that. I have spent this session cataloguing instruments whose zero means nothing — and here the guard against it fired on the harness's own first attempt. **The reading that was published is the one that survived its own control.**

The **planted-consumer control** is the other half and is the strongest sweep validation I have seen tonight: write a real reader of `EXPANDABLE_FIELD_TYPES` into `apps/console/src/`, re-run the identical command, **delta exactly one file**, remove it, re-run **byte-identical to the pre-plant listing, no residue**. Plus a population control proving `apps/` is inside the swept set at all (265 tracked files, zero hits for these names — and `createRoot` fires there on the same command shape). ⇒ the zero over `apps/` is a **reading**, not a dark grep.

## No pin, and the reasoning is the correct one

> a test asserting the docblock lacks `'renders as'` would be **a pin over a claim nobody reads**; a test asserting what `UserCellRenderer` prints belongs in `@object-ui/fields` — **where PR #8698 is already changing it and where it can fail.**

⭐ And the assertion that *was* observed to fail is the **reverse verification**: re-injecting the literal comment terminator the new docblock warns about (which the first draft genuinely contained) took type-check to exit 2 with 132 `error TS` lines, **the first at the injection site**. ⇒ `tsc` is proved to read the file, so the edit is inside a program rather than adjacent to one.

## Fences

⛔ Comment-only, no behaviour, nothing in `packages/fields`, nothing in the renderers. The changeset gate was observed **red before and green after** (its own verdict line quoted both ways), empty-frontmatter, `skip-changeset` correctly not applied. Lint narrowed to the one package **as a measurement**: `eslint.config.js` configures no `project`/`projectService`/`parserOptions`, so no type-aware rule exists and this diff **cannot** move an untouched file's verdict — stated with the reason rather than assumed.

objectui#8716 filed with the docblock's other uncheckable claims **listed rather than fixed**, per the card. The load-bearing one is worth reading: the server's expand path is *"the stated reason `user` is a member"* and this repo cannot reach it either.
